methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents grassroots institutional capacity-building in a non-metro region, creating potential for distributed deep learning if training translates to local application rather than talent export to NoVA.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's AI Ready RVA partnership concentrates academic-institutional AI capability in the state capital, potentially deepening Richmond's hub status but requiring intentional distribution mechanisms to avoid reinforcing metro-only expertise.

signals.title: New Jersey, Virginia Can Lead the Nation By Building ‘AI Resilience Cohorts’ to Develop Early-Career, State Talent Pipelines - Federation of American Scientists
signals.signal_reading: AI Resilience Cohorts proposal signals state-level infrastructure for distributed workforce development, potentially counteracting concentration by building early-career talent pipelines outside traditional tech hubs—execution determines whether deep or shallow.

signals.title: Residents share data center concerns with state senators during listening tour stop in Danville
signals.signal_reading: Danville residents expressing data center concerns without visible local AI capability development signals extraction without empowerment—infrastructure presence without workforce participation deepens regional exclusion from the AI economy.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: NBC's examination of who benefits from NoVA's data center boom exposes shallow community engagement even in the concentration zone—physical infrastructure without local capability diffusion suggests wealth extraction rather than distributed prosperity.
